sources.name: ExxonMobil product specifications and safety data sheets (Isopar sales specifications; No. 2 Diesel SDS)
sources.note: Isopar minimum flash points from the sales specifications (not SDSs): G 40 C (eff. 2018-06-11), H 49 C (2020-09-07), L 62 C (2015-04-01), M 93.5 C (2014-07-01); G and L aromatics max 0.01 wt%. The spec sheets forbid redistribution, so facts only. No. 2 Diesel SDS rev 2019-10-22: flash above 38 C, H351, for use as a motor fuel only (https://www.exxon.com/-/media/project/wep/exxon/exxon-retail-us/us-fuel-delivery/pdf/no-2-diesel-fuel-safety-data-sheet.pdf).

sources.name: Firefly Paraffin Lamp Oil Safety Data Sheet
sources.note: Revised 2023-10-10. C12-15 branched and linear alkanes above 95%, flash 83.5 C (182.3 F) closed cup, Flam. Liq. 4, H304, explosive mixture possible when sprayed or atomised, static accumulator, do not induce vomiting.

sources.name: Lamplight Farms safety data sheets (Ultra Pure and Medallion Lamp Oil; TIKI Citronella and Clean Burn Torch Fuels)
sources.note: Ultra Pure MSDS rev 3, 2007-01-09: flash 97 C (207 F), autoignition above 200 C, vapour pressure below 0.01 mmHg, not DOT regulated; internally inconsistent on appearance and odour. The 2002 Ultra Pure MSDS (121 C / 250 F, autoignition 216 C, freezes 8 C / 47 F) is read as reproduced in the Kindle Arts guidelines. Medallion SDS Rev 05, 2015-05-11: hydrotreated light distillate, flash 63 C / 145 F (https://media.lifeandhome.com/media/downloads/29778/41786953_SDS.pdf). TIKI Citronella Torch Fuel Rev 03 2015: flash 62.8-135 C, autoignition above 220 C. TIKI Clean Burn rev 2015-07-30: coconut fatty acid methyl esters, flash above 93.9 C. Medallion and TIKI citronella carry no static precaution.

sources.name: Zippo Lighter Fluid Safety Data Sheet (EU)
sources.note: Rev 2022-06-06. Same main CAS as Coleman camp fuel, flash below -6.5 C, autoignition above 200 C. The same sheet wrongly says fully miscible with water; SDSs can contain errors.

sources.name: Ronsonol Lighter Fluid Safety Data Sheet (EU)
sources.note: Rev 2018-01-19. C7-C9 hydrocarbons, CAS 64742-49-0, flash point 2 C closed cup, autoignition 260 C. The current US formula was not verified.

sources.name: Diggers Shellite Safety Data Sheet
sources.note: Issue 6, 2022-02-01 (NZ sheet). Flash -30 C (Abel), autoignition 280 C, n-hexane below 30%, recommended use solvent and lighter fuel, carcinogenicity 1A (H350), mutagenicity 1B (H340), H361f, STOT RE 1 (H372).

sources.name: Hunter's Shellite Safety Data Sheet
sources.note: January 2021. Heptane 32-36%, cyclohexane 25-27%, n-hexane 15-20%, flash -15 C.

sources.name: Sterno Methanol Gel, Handy Fuel Safety Data Sheet
sources.note: Rev 2013-05-14, hosted by Durham Tech. Methanol 50-100%, H301/H311/H331/H370. Official SDS index: https://www.sterno.com/pages/sds-1

sources.name: Chemfax Methanol/Methyl Hydrate Safety Data Sheet
sources.note: Version 7, 2021-01-25. Methanol 100%, flash 12 C. Cited for the fact that Canadian methyl hydrate is methanol.

sources.name: Aspen 4 Safety Data Sheet (GB)
sources.note: Version 1.0, issued 2022-11-08. Alkylate petrol, fuel for 4-stroke motors, flash point -45 C, H224. This is the alkylatbensin that Swedish stove-fuel lists name; it is petrol, never a spinning fuel.

sources.name: Safety Data Sheet, Mehron Spirit Gum 118
sources.note: Named product sheet, revised 2017-04-28: SD alcohol, shellac and ethyl acetate; flash point 54 F closed cup, so ignitable vapour while wet.

sources.name: The Woolmark Company
sources.note: Wool is fire resistant fact sheet citing CSIRO: LOI 25.2 wool, 18.4 cotton; ignition 570-600 C against 255 C. The wool industry's own body, an interested party; the guide says so in the text.

sources.name: Coats fire and heat resistant threads
sources.note: Thread maker's guide: nylon and polyester seams weaken around 350 F, cotton thread to be avoided near fire, aramid thread.

sources.name: American and Efird (A&E) technical bulletins
sources.note: Thread maker. Corespun versus Spun Poly Threads: a corespun thread is a continuous-filament polyester core, about 60% of the thread, wrapped in staple cotton or polyester.

sources.name: Dritz sewing notions product listings
sources.note: Braided elastic 9332B listed as 55% polyester, 45% rubber (checked 2026-09-24). Cite the named product, not Dritz generically.

sources.name: Levi Strauss and Co.
sources.note: Denim terminology guide: stretch denim is 1 to 3 percent elastane.

sources.name: Gildan
sources.note: Heavy Cotton G5000 fibre content by colour (solids 100% cotton, Sport Grey 90/10, Ash 99/1, heathers 50/50), checked 2026-09-24; a snapshot that can change.

sources.name: YKK Americas
sources.note: Organic cotton tape zipper listing: tape 45% cotton, 46% corespun, 9% polyester.

sources.name: Kaneka Corporation
sources.note: Kanekalon braiding and wig fibre is a modacrylic. Its flame-retardant claims are the maker's own and are not repeated as fact.

sources.name: The LYCRA Company
sources.note: Maker's description of COOLMAX as a polyester fibre.

sources.name: Ultrasuede
sources.note: Ultrasuede ST: polyester microfibre non-woven with a polyurethane binder.

sources.name: Naugahyde
sources.note: Maker describes itself as the predominant brand in vinyl-coated fabrics.

sources.name: Nike
sources.note: Help page describing Dri-FIT as a polycotton fabric; cited only to show Dri-FIT is a technology name that still means polyester.

sources.name: Tyndale
sources.note: FR clothing maker's explanation of NFPA 2112 pass/fail tests (500 F for 5 minutes, no ignite/melt/drip/separate, 10 percent shrinkage), used because the standard is paywalled.

sources.name: Firwin
sources.note: Industrial insulation maker: hook-and-loop hooks are nylon or polyester, tolerating about 280 F (138 C).

sources.name: North American Fire Arts Association Performer Safety Guidelines
sources.note: Revision 3.0, as reprinted by the Eagle River Fire Protection District (Colorado), revised January 2019, hosted on the Town of Avon site. Voluntary guidelines written as should, supplementing NFPA 160; not a federal work. Flame toxicity (petroleum fuels always toxic, worse indoors and in semi-enclosed low-wind spots), backstage fuel station (outside behind a hard wall, 30 ft from audience and smoking), extinguisher at least class B, ABC preferred; wick attachment through wick and device, never glue or friction; shafted tools fireproof or covered 4 in beyond the flame zone; tempered-metal connectors for multi-part props; tug test, any wear is a failure; check each costume part and practise lit in costume; spotters dressed with equal care. Revision 2.1 (2005), reprinted in the Utah compilation, is superseded.

sources.name: Burning Man Fire Conclave, Fire Tools and Safety
sources.note: Dated 2021-03-20. Fuel list (including Naptha as a white gas alias), containers, 5 lb ABC extinguisher, never dump fuel.

sources.name: Burning Man fire art safety agreements: Fuel and Hazardous Materials Storage
sources.note: Undated page, accessed 2026-09-24. 10 ft from combustibles (shade structures and tents named) and ignition sources, 25 ft from open flames while filling, 110% secondary containment, shade allowed over propane but not liquid fuel storage, 110 gal camp cap.

sources.name: Kindle Arts Society Fire Performance Guidelines, Version 207
sources.note: January 2015, British Columbia. White gas or lamp oil before kerosene; hinged-lid barrel fuel depot. Reproduces an older Coleman MSDS (mists flammable below flash point), an Imperial Oil kerosene SDS (40 C) and the 2002 Lamplight Ultra Pure lamp oil MSDS (121 C, freezes 8 C).

sources.name: Sewing and Craft Alliance
sources.note: Guideline 4.107, Identifying Fibers and Fabrics (11/08): safe burn-test method and results by fibre, and its warning that blends cannot be identified with certainty. A trade association, not a standards body; listed under not-authorities in the guide.

sources.name: Australian and New Zealand Committee on Resuscitation (ANZCOR)
sources.publisher: Australian Resuscitation Council and New Zealand Resuscitation Council

sources.name: Agromisa Foundation, Agrodok series
sources.note: Agrodok 40, Small-scale mushroom cultivation (Oei, 2005), is a practical manual for growing oyster, shiitake and wood ear mushrooms at small scale. Copyrighted: restate the fact, never the wording.

sources.name: UF/IFAS Extension
sources.publisher: University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences
sources.note: EDIS publications, among them SS662, a home guide to growing oyster mushrooms on straw. A state university: restate the fact. AN239, Raising Backyard Chickens for Eggs, by Henry, Ryals, Halbritter and Barber (published 18 January 2024), read 2026-10-04 at https://ask.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/AN239: ordinances, roosters and slaughter in residential areas; 3 square feet of house and 8 to 10 of run per bird; hardware cloth and fencing buried 12 to 18 inches in an L; nest boxes; starter 20-24, grower 16-20, layer 14-16 percent protein with 3.5 to 4 percent calcium, kidney problems and rickets in chicks fed layer feed; medicated feed and the coccidiosis vaccine; grit versus calcium; foods never to feed; pesticides and eggs; 25 hens a gallon a day; 200 to 240 eggs a hen a year; 14 to 16 hours of light with lights off part of the night; the moult; nests checked daily; washing at 90 F and 20 F warmer, dried and refrigerated at or below 45 F; straight run about half male; brooding at 90 to 95 F down 5 F a week; compost and the 131 F benchmark; 50 feet from water; mortality and burial at two feet under Florida law. Its 6 to 8 week egg shelf life is not used (the FDA says 3 weeks for best quality).

sources.name: Cornell Small Farms Program
sources.note: Hosts Methods of Commercial Mushroom Cultivation in the Northeastern United States and the log-grown shiitake best management practices manual. The manual itself is copyright the University of Vermont (see uvm-extension).

sources.name: University of Vermont Extension
sources.note: Its Center for Sustainable Agriculture holds the copyright on Best Management Practices for Log-Based Shiitake Cultivation in the Northeastern United States (2013, with Cornell). Its Northwest Crops and Soils team publishes on soil nitrogen.

sources.name: Cornell University Nutrient Management Spear Program
sources.note: Agronomy Fact Sheet series, including number 48 on deriving lime rates from buffer pH.

sources.name: Clemson Cooperative Extension
sources.note: Home and Garden Information Center fact sheets, and the Agricultural Service Laboratory soil testing pages. The HGIC site answers automated clients with a Cloudflare challenge while serving browsers normally.

sources.name: Oregon State University Extension Service
sources.note: Its Pacific Northwest publications, such as EC 1560 on acidifying soil west of the Cascades, apply directly to the Puget Sound locale. PNW 565, Why Did My Chickens Stop Laying?, by James Hermes (Pacific Northwest Extension: Oregon State, Washington State and Idaho; published January 2003, reviewed 2023), read 2026-10-04 at https://extension.oregonstate.edu/catalog/pnw-565-why-did-my-chickens-stop-laying: laying from 18 to 20 weeks, peak at about 35 weeks above 90 percent for about 10 weeks; 265 eggs a year from a commercial Leghorn, backyard breeds fewer; 14 to 16 hours of light bright enough to read a newspaper, never lapsing; the moult and the six-week winter rest in the second winter; broodiness; laying well to 2 or 3 years, prolapse; layer ration and oyster shell free choice, treats to 15 minutes; starter or grower feed not for layers, partly because medications in starter diets may leave residues in eggs; stresses. Its lab phone numbers date from 2003 and are not used.

sources.name: University of Delaware Cooperative Extension

sources.name: Washington State Department of Ecology
sources.note: A state agency; Washington does not waive copyright in state works by statute (see schemas/source.toml), so facts only. Runs the Tacoma Smelter Plume cleanup and the Dirt Alert map of arsenic and lead in Puget Sound soils. Well construction law administered by Ecology, read 2026-10-04 for Wells and Groundwater and Water and Wind Power: RCW 90.44.050 (the groundwater permit exemption, and an exempt withdrawal, as far as regularly used beneficially, carrying a right equal to one from a permit), RCW 90.44.020 (the groundwater chapter supplements chapter 90.03 and extends it to groundwater) and RCW 90.03.010 (as between appropriations, the earlier first; these two read after the 2026-10-04 fact check), RCW 90.94.030 (WRIA 15 and the other streamflow restoration watersheds: $500, 950 gallons a day, 350 in a drought emergency, until rules say otherwise), RCW 18.104 (18.104.030 unlawful acts including drilling without a needed permit; 18.104.048 72 hours' notice; 18.104.180 the self-build exemption), RCW 90.03.250 (a permit before using or diverting surface water), and WAC 173-160 (141 well reports; 171 siting and setbacks; 231 surface seals; 261 dug wells; 291 the upper terminal; 301 temporary capping; 321 pump tests; 381 decommissioning). Facts only, as for every Washington source.

sources.name: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries
sources.note: A state agency; Washington does not waive copyright in state works by statute (see schemas/source.toml), so facts only, restated. Runs electrical licensing, permits and inspections under chapter 19.28 RCW and chapter 296-46B WAC. Read 2026-10-04 for Where Your Own Electrical Work Stops (statutes and rules at app.leg.wa.gov the same day): RCW 19.28.006 (class A basic electrical work, the like-in-kind replacement of a breaker, fuse, residential light fitting, lamp, snap switch, dimmer, receptacle, thermostat and other listed parts; class B; like-in-kind means similar voltage, current draw and function in the same location), 19.28.010 (utility-owned equipment between the meter base and the meter exempt from the chapter), 19.28.041 (an electrical contractor licence to carry on the business), 19.28.101 (inspection; no permit for class A basic work unless deficiencies require inspection; nothing concealed before approval; inspection and approval before asking the utility to connect), 19.28.131 (penalties of $50 to $10,000 for violating 19.28.010 to .141 and .311 to .361), 19.28.161 (certificates of competency), 19.28.261 (the owner exemption at a residence, farm, place of business or other owned property, not for a new building for rent, sale or lease or property sold within 12 months of acquiring it, a narrow exception for up to four units; help from friends, neighbours and relatives not in the trade); WAC 296-46B-010 (the 2023 National Electrical Code adopted, the 2026 edition from 31 December 2026; inspectors interpret but do not lay out work; materials listed or meeting recognised product standards). L&I pages, undated: Purchase Permits and Request Inspections (https://lni.wa.gov/licensing-permits/electrical/electrical-permits-fees-and-inspections/purchase-permits-request-inspections: owners buy a permit only for their own work on their own property and are strongly encouraged to hire an electrical contractor; a hired contractor buys the permit; contact the serving utility before disconnection, reconnection or first connection; permits good for 1 year; request inspection before burying or concealing anything and no later than 3 business days after completing the work or 1 business day after any part is energized; do not cover work before inspection), and City Electrical Permits and Inspections (https://lni.wa.gov/licensing-permits/electrical/electrical-permits-fees-and-inspections/city-electrical-permits-inspections: 25 cities and Tacoma Power issue permits and inspect for themselves; none in Kitsap County, so Silverdale is L&I's). Property Owner Electrical Work Permit Application, form F500-094-000, dated 07-2026 (https://www.lni.wa.gov/forms-publications/F500-094-000.pdf: only licensed electrical contractors employing certified electricians may do electrical work, owners may apply for the exemption with an affidavit before starting; the owner's name on the deed; agents, managers and relatives cannot buy the permit for the owner; a lessee needs a lease giving permission, WAC 296-46B-925(13)). Added after the 2026-10-04 fact check: RCW 19.28.131's penalty applies to any person, firm, partnership, corporation or other entity violating RCW 19.28.010 to 19.28.141 or 19.28.311 to 19.28.361, so owners as well as contractors (for example, covering work before inspection, 19.28.101); the Purchase Permits page also says failing to request an inspection may result in civil penalties. WAC 296-46B-901(7)(b) (https://app.leg.wa.gov/WAC/default.aspx?cite=296-46B-901, read 2026-10-04): the class A basic electrical work exempt from permits includes at most five snap switches, dimmers, receptacle outlets, thermostats, heating elements, or luminaire ballasts or LED drivers. WAC 296-46B-406 was repealed in 2014 and 296-46B-406R in 2024 (chapter section list, read 2026-10-04), so Washington has no current amendment of NEC article 406 and the 2023 code's replacement-receptacle rule should apply as published (our reading; the code text itself was not read). About Electrical Installations (https://lni.wa.gov/licensing-permits/electrical/, undated, read 2026-10-04) is the Electrical Program's landing page for property owners, used as the locale mapping's address.

sources.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.note: Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56 (Allen, Pereira, Raes and Smith, Crop evapotranspiration, 1998) is the standard method for crop water use: reference evapotranspiration times a crop coefficient. Its front matter reserves all rights (copyright FAO, 1998), so facts only, although FAO puts the full text online (https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e00.htm). Irrigation Water Management Training Manual 4, Irrigation Scheduling (1989), Annex I, gives indicative field application efficiencies. Newer FAO works may carry a CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO licence instead: check each one. Codex Standard for Named Animal Fats, CODEX-STAN 211-1999, in Codex Alimentarius Volume 8, Fats, Oils and Related Products, second edition (revised 2001), FAO and WHO, Rome 2001 (https://www.fao.org/4/y2774e/y2774e05.htm, read 2026-10-04 for Soap, Lye and Cleaning): saponification value in mg KOH per g of fat, lard and rendered pork fat 192 to 203, premier jus 190 to 200, edible tallow 190 to 202. Codex texts are FAO copyright: facts only.

sources.name: Kansas State University Research and Extension
sources.note: Alam and Rogers, Tensiometer Use in Scheduling Irrigation, L-796: what tensiometer readings mean for each soil texture and when to start irrigating. A copy is hosted by Washington State University Extension.

sources.name: Nebraska Extension
sources.note: Rain barrel guide G2220, which recommends against using rain barrel water on fruit and vegetable gardens (other extension services disagree; see rutgers-njaes). G1724, Egg Cleaning Procedures for the Backyard Flock, by Sok and Scheideler (issued June 2007), read 2026-10-04 at https://extensionpubs.unl.edu/publication/g1724/html/view: a nest for every four to five hens; eggs gathered at least daily; dirty eggs washed in water at least 20 F (11 C) warmer than the eggs, 90 to 120 F, not soaked. G2018, Bloat Prevention and Treatment in Cattle, by Rasby, Waechter-Mead and Redfern, revised 2024 (https://extensionpubs.unl.edu/publication/g2018/pdf/view, read 2026-10-04): rumen gas after meals mostly belched out; signs (left-side distension, stamping and kicking at the belly, laboured breathing, frequent urination and defecation, collapse); alfalfa and many clovers; a consistent, steady diet; never turning hungry animals onto high-risk pasture, filling them with dry hay, avoiding wet pasture, waiting three to five days after frost; grain-rich rations, bloat and acidosis; plan with the vet before the grazing season; never drench a bloated animal. Its tube, needle and trocar instructions are deliberately not taught in the Library.

A trade-magazine column by a university specialist, not a peer-reviewed paper. Already cited by data/garden/lighting.ron.

sources.note: Federal regulation text, quotable. 10 CFR 430.32(d) sets the minimum uniform energy factor for residential water heaters, with a stricter table for heaters made on or after 6 May 2029. Also cited (read 2026-10-03): 29 CFR 1910.147 and 1910.333(b)(2)(iv), lockout and verifying that a circuit is de-energised with test equipment; 21 CFR 112.161-112.165, what a farm record must contain and how long it is kept; 14 CFR 43.9, maintenance record entries; 7 CFR 205.103, organic recordkeeping. Cite the section and the date it was read, because the eCFR is updated in place. Also cited (read 2026-10-03): 29 CFR 1910.212 (machine guarding), 1910.242(b) (compressed air for cleaning under 30 psi), 1910.244(a) (jacks: block a raised load at once; tag a jack that is out of order), 1926.651 and 1926.652 (locating utilities before digging; cave-in protection below 5 feet; spoil 2 feet from the edge), 1926.1053(b) (ladder use, the one-quarter rule); 24 CFR 3285.203 (manufactured home site drainage, one half inch per foot for the first ten feet). Added after the fact check (read 2026-10-03): 1910.147(e)(2)(i) and (ii) (everyone safely positioned or removed, and affected employees told, before a machine is restarted); 1910.244(a)(1)(i) and (a)(2)(i) (a jack rated to lift and sustain the load; its base blocked without a firm foundation); 1926.650(b) (competent person defined); 1926.651(b)(3) (the exact location of underground installations found by safe and acceptable means as digging approaches the estimate) and (j)(2) (spoil 2 feet back, or retaining devices); 1926.1053(b)(3), (10), (11) and (13) (rated capacity, both rails supported equally, not moved while occupied, the top or top step of a stepladder not a step); 1926.252(e) (oily rags in fire resistant covered containers); 1910.266(d)(1)(iv) to (vii) and (e)(2)(i) (chainsaw leg, foot, head and eye protection; chain brake, kickback devices never disabled). Also cited (read 2026-10-03): 16 CFR 255.2 (FTC Endorsement Guides, consumer endorsements: a testimonial on a key attribute is read as the typical result; the heat pump example) and 29 CFR 1926.302(e)(1) (powder-actuated tools operated only by people trained on the particular tool). Also read 2026-10-03 (eCFR up to date as of 1 October 2026): 49 CFR 571.111, Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 111, Rear visibility, S5.4.2: a convex mirror used to meet S5.3 is marked "Objects in Mirror Are Closer Than They Appear." The versioner API needs an Accept-Encoding header that allows compression. Also cited (read 2026-10-03): 29 CFR 1910.95, occupational noise exposure (Table G-16, 90 dBA for 8 hours to 115 dBA for a quarter of an hour, halving at 5 dB; impulsive or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak; the 85 dBA action level for a hearing conservation program; Appendix B, subtract 7 dB from the NRR for A-weighted levels). Also read 2026-10-03 (eCFR title 29 issue of 30 September 2026): 29 CFR 1910.184, slings ((c) safe operating practices, including no knots to shorten, rated capacities, no shock loading, hands clear while tightening, everyone kept clear of loads about to be lifted and of suspended loads; (d) daily inspection by a competent person; (e)(2)(i) attachments rated at least equal to the chain, or the sling limited to the rated capacity of the weakest component; (f)(5)(vii) wire rope slings removed from service for corrosion; (h)(5)(v) fibre rope slings for discoloration or rotting; (i)(9) synthetic web slings for acid or caustic burns, melting or charring) and 29 CFR 1926.1053(a)(12) (wood ladders not coated with any opaque covering, except labels on one face of a side rail) and (b)(16) (portable ladders with corroded components marked defective or tagged "Do Not Use" and withdrawn until repaired). Also read 2026-10-04 (versioner API, issue of 1 October 2026): 7 CFR 56.76(f)(3) and (f)(9) (egg wash water at 90 F or higher and at least 20 F warmer than the inside of the eggs, printed with the conversion slip "20 °F (6.7 °C)", which is the size of 20 F read as a temperature (-6.7 C) rather than as a difference: a difference of 20 F is about 11.1 C; "Eggs shall not be allowed to stand or soak in water."); 21 CFR 118.1(a) (the egg safety rule covers producers with 3,000 or more laying hens at a farm that does not sell all its eggs directly to consumers); 7 CFR 205.203(c)(1) and (2) (raw manure incorporated 120 or 90 days before harvest; compost with an initial C:N ratio between 25:1 and 40:1, then at 131 to 170 F for 3 days in-vessel or static aerated, or 15 days in a windrow turned five times); 16 CFR 1302 (Ban of Extremely Flammable Contact Adhesives, published 19 December 1977, effective 18 January 1978: flash point at or below 20 F and containers over half a pint among the tests; the 1302.5 findings on vapour ignited by pilot lights, space heaters, refrigerator motor and wall outlet sparks and friction, often in another part of the house; a pint as a substantial explosion hazard; labelling inadequate; flammable, non-flammable (chlorinated) and water-based alternatives, water-based ones drying slowly, or perhaps never, in very humid weather).
